items.title: Realtor.com lead dispute heads to closed-door arbitration after appeal fails
items.description: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals has upheld a lower court’s ruling to send real estate agent plaintiffs’ claims that Realtor.com parent company Move sold them allegedly fake leads, to arbitration. Earlier this week, the Ninth Circuit declined the plaintiffs’ petition to rehear the appeal en banc. This comes after the appeals court dismissed the initial appeal in mid-August, writing in their ruling that despite the lower court ordering the parties to arbitration and dismissing the suit , that this ruling was not a final, appealable judgement. Originally filed in the August of 2024 , the suit, which was filed by lead plaintiff James Bandy, claims that many of the leads the real estate agent plaintiffs received from Realtor.com were fake, nonexistent or failed to meet expectations. While Judge Stanley Blumenfeld did dismiss the lawsuit, in his ruling he said the dismissal was “functionally indistinguishable from a stay,” allowing the parties to reopen the case after arbitration if the court needed to review or enforce the outcome. Due to this, the appeals court found that the ruling was not a final decision that ended the litigation, preventing them from having appellate jurisdiction. If the parties now move to arbitration as Judge Blumenfeld ordered, the proceedings will mostly be blocked from public view. Additional defendants in the lawsuit include National Association of Realtors (NAR), Move Sales, Inc. , OpCity, Inc. , OpCity Acquisition, LLC , RIN and RealSelect. Related More: Move Realtor.com

items.title: Kroenke Announces $135M Renovation For Denver's Ball Arena
items.description: Kroenke Announces $135M Renovation For Denver's Ball Arena September 18, 2026 | 5:06 pm ET Cassidy Ritter, Denver Another Denver sports complex is getting an upgrade. Kroenke Sports Entertainment, owner of the Colorado Avalanche and Denver Nuggets , announced plans on Sept. 18 to renovate Ball Arena . KSE will spend an estimated $135M on renovations at the 27-year-old facility, according to a statement from the Avalanche . Kroenke Sports Entertainment A rendering of Kroenke Sports Entertainment's renovated Ball Arena Renovations include three new clubs inside and a 30K SF addition to the arena’s east lobby, which will include a team store double the size of the current retail shop. A 34K SF pedestrian plaza will also face Chopper Circle, according to The Denver Post . Ball Arena’s upgrades come about a year and a half after KSE revealed plans to redevelop parking lots surrounding the facility . Redevelopment plans call for an entertainment venue, hotel, two multifamily buildings, a central park, shopping, dining and office towers, according to past Bisnow reporting and a statement from the Avalanche. “The renovated Ball Arena and the subsequent redevelopment of the surrounding land allow us to keep doing both for another 25 years and beyond,” KSE Chairman Stan Kroenke said in a statement. Construction at Ball Arena is expected to begin next summer and end in the fall of 2028, according to The Denver Post. The indoor sports arena opened as the Pepsi Center in 1999. Ball Corp . purchased the arena’s naming rights in 2020. The facility houses the Avalanche, Nuggets and Colorado Mammoth, all of which are owned by Kroenke. Denverites have long wondered when KSE would upgrade Ball Arena, especially as other Denver sports teams announced new stadiums. Denver Summit FC, the city’s professional women’s soccer team, will build a $225M open-air stadium in Santa Fe Yards. The stadium was expected to open ahead of the 2028 season, but delays pushed the opening back to later in the year. The team is playing at a temporary stadium it built in Centennial. The Denver Broncos are also expected to build a new stadium at Burnham Yards, south of the team’s current stadium. Last month, additional details and renderings for the proposed entertainment district surrounding the Broncos’ potential new stadium were released. In addition to the three teams that play at Ball Arena, Kroenke owns the Colorado Rapids and recently bought a controlling stake in the Los Angeles Angels . KSE also took full ownership of Denver’s River Mile development , a project that includes Elitch Gardens and Meow Wolf, in June 2025. items.title: Builder Sentiment Falls on Higher Interest Rates and Costs – NAHB
items.description: Builder Sentiment Falls on Higher Interest Rates and Costs – Eye On Housing Skip to content Search Research/Data Housing Economics Plus Books Dashboards Local Data Research Studies Services Indices Team Videos Research/Data Housing Economics Plus Books Dashboards Local Data Research Studies Services Indices Team Videos Eye On Housing National Association of Home Builders Economic Research Blog Builder Sentiment Falls on Higher Interest Rates and Costs September 16, 2026 Robert Dietz No Comments Higher mortgage rates, worsening labor shortages and rising material costs are weighing on builder sentiment. Builder confidence in the market for newly built single-family homes fell three points to 32 in September, according to the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI) released today. Buyer traffic has weakened across much of the country, largely because of rising mortgage rates. Builders also continue to face higher material costs, rising gas and diesel prices and persistent labor shortages. In some markets, builders report that increased immigration enforcement is discouraging legal workers from reporting to job sites. The HMI shows builder confidence at its lowest level since September 2025, as tight lending conditions and elevated land, labor and construction costs persist. Notably, 42% of builders rated current lot availability as poor and 38% as fair. The latest HMI survey found that 38% of builders cut prices in September, up from 35% in August. The average price cut remained at 6% for the sixth consecutive month. Meanwhile, 66% of builders reported using sales incentives in September, up from 63% in August and the highest share since 67% posted in December. Derived from a monthly survey that NAHB has been conducting for more than 40 years, the NAHB/Wells Fargo HMI gauges builder perceptions of current single-family home sales and sales expectations for the next six months as “good,” “fair” or “poor.” The survey also asks builders to rate traffic of prospective buyers as “high to very high,” “average” or “low to very low.” Scores for each component are then used to calculate a seasonally adjusted index where any number over 50 indicates that more builders view conditions as good than poor. The index measuring current sales conditions in September fell four points to 35, the index gauging future sales expectations dropped six points to 37 and the index charting prospective buyer traffic held steady at 23. Looking at the three-month moving averages for regional HMI scores, the Midwest dropped one point to 44, the Northeast fell five points to 39, the South fell one point to 31 and the West posted a one-point gain to 28. The HMI tables can be found at nahb.org/hmi .
